title: gap:M0:L_rt_go_v0: M0's whole-header round trip dec_go(enc_sol(h)) = some(view(h)) at version 0 has no M3 law to pair with
outside: No catalog rule states a whole-record round trip. PAR's round_trip producer (P1) states one law per E1 inverse atom (encoder, getter, version): L_par_rt_enc_sol_BatchHeaderBytes_<F>_v0, 11 at version 0: ten of view's fields plus BlobCommitHash, which reads the blobVersionedHash slot. All of them are PROVED. None covers the slot enc_sol fills with a constant: SequencerSetVerifyHash, written as bytes32(0) whatever the header, a field M3's R_Header does not have. That slot is an E2 constant read, not an inverse atom: I25's par_lossy lists (CODEC.enc_sol, CODEC.BatchHeaderBytes_SequencerSetVerifyHash) at version 0 as constant_read, covered false (gen/M3/par_lossy/header_length.json). spec/M3/lib/backtest_map.json gives dec_go and view no image, so B2 cannot pair the row (results/M3/backtest.json).

name: PAR_record_round_trip

basis.argument: An encoder enc into a byte record, and a decoder given as a family of getters {G} valid at version N, satisfy dec(enc(h)) = some(view_N(h)) iff every getter of the family returns, on enc(h), the value view_N gives its slot. The encoder fills each slot in one of two ways. From a record field F: PAR's round_trip law G(enc(h)) == Some(h.F) states it. With a constant c it writes whatever h is: the constant read-back law G(enc(h)) == Some(c) states it. The record law is the conjunction over the whole family at version N, under the version pin. It adds no premise, because a constant slot has no field on the encoder's record. Under mu, the source's Header maps to the record by forgetting the constant slots, dec_go maps to the getter family, and view maps to the getter tuple in view's order with each constant slot mapped to its constant. The source's own premise (M0: sequencerSetVerifyHash = 0) equates view's slot with c. So each B3 bridge is one implication, and it is refuted where the source lacks that premise. Getters outside view (BlobCommitHash) only add conjuncts on M3's side.
basis.obligation: Per instance, at version N: (1) every round_trip law L_par_rt_enc_sol_BatchHeaderBytes_<F>_vN of the family, decided PROVED (all are, today); (2) a constant read-back law for each constant slot, here L_par_rt_enc_sol_BatchHeaderBytes_SequencerSetVerifyHash_vN, stating BatchHeaderBytes_SequencerSetVerifyHash(enc_sol(pin_h(h))) == Some(32 zero bytes), decided PROVED; (3) coverage: every BatchHeaderBytes getter valid at version N has a component, checked against the extracted getter family, not against the laws that exist; (4) the record law, generated from (1)-(3) by the producer on a new catalog version and checked by Bend; (5) the mu amendment above, with the B3 bridge to M0's L_rt_go_vN decided on the compiled models.

notes: Drafted by the queue runner from F-M3-08, with approval null: no agent approves. F-M3-08 is the only finding on these gaps, so L7 (a)'s two distinct findings are not met yet.

title: A codec bug that misaligns an encoder and its decoder (an off-by-one offset, a wrong version guard) leaves no rule obligation stating their round trip
outside: PAR's round-trip and pinned cross-component obligations are instantiated from evidence atoms (E1 inverse atoms, the Go basis of G4) that the evidence pass computes from the layouts of the very code being checked; a misaligned pair has no such evidence, so the rule as instantiated states nothing about it and the defect is outside every obligation HOLON derives (whitepaper §5.1: obligations need evidence at least medium).
